summary: The root قسس (qss) primarily refers to hardness or rigidity, like a hard heart. It also relates to being old or aged, and to a Christian priest, perhaps due to their venerable age or strictness.

headwords.gloss: A calumniator; a slanderer; one who inquires respecting news, and then makes it known, divulges it, or tells it, in a malicious or mischievous manner, so as to occasion discord, dissension, or the like

parts.t: one who inquires respecting news, and then makes it known, divulges it, or tells it, in a malicious or mischievous manner, so as to occasion discord, dissension, or the like,

headwords.def: قَسَّاسٌ A calumniator; a slanderer: (M:) or one who inquires respecting news, and then makes it known, divulges it, or tells it, in a malicious or mischievous manner, so as to occasion discord, dissension, or the like, (TA, voce قَتَّاتٌ .)

headwords.gloss: A seeker; one who seeks repeatedly; leisurely, without inadvertence

parts.t: One who inquires respecting the affairs of others.

headwords.def: قَسْقَاسٌ A seeker, or one who seeks repeatedly or leisurely, without inadvertence; as also . (TA.) One who inquires respecting the affairs of others. (M.)
